scene.label: Act 4, Scene 2
scene.title: SCENE II. Athens. A Room in Quince's House
scene.location: Athens. A Room in Quince's House

content.text: Enter Quince, Flute, Snout and Starveling.

lines.text: Have you sent to Bottom's house? Is he come home yet?
lines.plainText: Have you sent to Bottom's house Is he come home yet

lines.text: He cannot be heard of. Out of doubt he is transported.
lines.plainText: He cannot be heard of Out of doubt he is transported

lines.text: If he come not, then the play is marred. It goes not forward, doth it?
lines.plainText: If he come not then the play is marred It goes not forward doth it

lines.text: It is not possible. You have not a man in all Athens able to discharge Pyramus but he.
lines.plainText: It is not possible You have not a man in all Athens able to discharge Pyramus but he

lines.text: No, he hath simply the best wit of any handicraft man in Athens.
lines.plainText: No he hath simply the best wit of any handicraft man in Athens

lines.text: Yea, and the best person too, and he is a very paramour for a sweet voice.
lines.plainText: Yea and the best person too and he is a very paramour for a sweet voice

lines.text: You must say paragon. A paramour is, God bless us, a thing of naught.
lines.plainText: You must say paragon A paramour is God bless us a thing of naught

lines.text: Masters, the Duke is coming from the temple, and there is two or three lords and ladies more married. If our sport had gone forward, we had all been made men.
lines.plainText: Masters the Duke is coming from the temple and there is two or three lords and ladies more married If our sport had gone forward we had all been made men

lines.text: O sweet bully Bottom! Thus hath he lost sixpence a day during his life; he could not have 'scaped sixpence a day. An the Duke had not given him sixpence a day for playing Pyramus, I'll be hanged. He would have deserved it: sixpence a day in Pyramus, or nothing.
lines.plainText: O sweet bully Bottom Thus hath he lost sixpence a day during his life he could not have 'scaped sixpence a day An the Duke had not given him sixpence a day for playing Pyramus I'll be hanged He would have deserved it sixpence a day in Pyramus or nothing

lines.text: Where are these lads? Where are these hearts?
lines.plainText: Where are these lads Where are these hearts

lines.text: Bottom! O most courageous day! O most happy hour!
lines.plainText: Bottom O most courageous day O most happy hour

lines.text: Masters, I am to discourse wonders: but ask me not what; for if I tell you, I am not true Athenian. I will tell you everything, right as it fell out.
lines.plainText: Masters I am to discourse wonders but ask me not what for if I tell you I am not true Athenian I will tell you everything right as it fell out

lines.text: Not a word of me. All that I will tell you is, that the Duke hath dined. Get your apparel together, good strings to your beards, new ribbons to your pumps; meet presently at the palace; every man look o'er his part. For the short and the long is, our play is preferred. In any case, let Thisbe have clean linen; and let not him that plays the lion pare his nails, for they shall hang out for the lion's claws. And most dear actors, eat no onions nor garlick, for we are to utter sweet breath; and I do not doubt but to hear them say it is a sweet comedy. No more words. Away! Go, away!
